name: cantoria
description: Sings the lyrics of a score for notation extensions such as Lily#: notes with syllables in, a voice out, through DiffSinger voices in the OpenUtau format, or your own NEUTRINO or VOICEVOX. Voices from different engines can sing together. Open source (Apache-2.0); runs locally.
author: Yoshifumi Tsuda

cantoria.defaultFemaleVoice.markdownDescription:
The voice that sings a female part when the score names no voice, as `engine/name` (`neutrino/MERROW`, `diffsinger/TIGER`). Empty: the first installed voice that says it is female and sings the words' language.

**[Choose a voice…](command:cantoria.chooseFemaleVoice)**

cantoria.defaultMaleVoice.markdownDescription:
The voice that sings a male part when the score names no voice, as `engine/name`. Empty: the first installed voice that says it is male and sings the words' language.

**[Choose a voice…](command:cantoria.chooseMaleVoice)**

cantoria.gpu.markdownDescription: Render on the GPU where the engine can: NEUTRINO through CUDA, a DiffSinger voice through DirectML (any DirectX 12 GPU; the CPU stands in where there is none). Off: the CPU, slower by an order of magnitude.

cantoria.cacheSizeMB.markdownDescription: The disk, in megabytes, that rendered voices and their phrases may take together. Past it, what has gone unused longest is removed and rendered again when it is next needed. A three-minute voice takes about 33 MB: 16 MB of phrases and 16 MB for the voice laid together.

cantoria.voicesFolder.markdownDescription:
The folder whose subfolders are DiffSinger voices in the OpenUtau format (each holding a `dsconfig.yaml`, as OpenUtau installs them). Each voice is its author's work under its author's terms; none is bundled. Empty: no DiffSinger voice can be sung.

**[Choose the folder…](command:cantoria.chooseVoicesFolder)**

cantoria.vocoderFolder.markdownDescription:
A vocoder folder (holding `vocoder.yaml` and its model) for DiffSinger voices that bundle none. Most voices bundle their own; leave this empty then.

**[Choose the folder…](command:cantoria.chooseVocoderFolder)**

cantoria.neutrinoFolder.markdownDescription:
The folder of your NEUTRINO installation (Tau, v3.2 or later): the one holding `bin\`, `model\` and `settings\`. NEUTRINO is not bundled — it is free software of STUDIO NEUTRINO under its own terms, from [studio-neutrino.com](https://studio-neutrino.com/). Empty: no NEUTRINO voice can be sung (a DiffSinger voices folder is the other engine).

**[Choose the folder…](command:cantoria.chooseNeutrinoFolder)**

cantoria.voicevoxFolder.markdownDescription:
The folder of your VOICEVOX (holding `vv-engine\run.exe`). Set: when a score or the list of voices needs a VOICEVOX voice and no VOICEVOX is running, Cantoria starts its engine on a port of its own and stops it when VS Code closes. A VOICEVOX you opened yourself is used and left alone. You use VOICEVOX under [its terms](https://voicevox.hiroshiba.jp/term/). Empty: Cantoria starts nothing, and only a VOICEVOX you have opened sings.

**[Choose the folder…](command:cantoria.chooseVoicevoxFolder)**

cantoria.voicevoxUrl.markdownDescription: Where the running VOICEVOX answers. Start VOICEVOX and its singing voices are listed; Japanese only. VOICEVOX is not bundled: get it from [voicevox.hiroshiba.jp](https://voicevox.hiroshiba.jp/). Each character has its own terms, and a published work credits `VOICEVOX:name`. Empty: VOICEVOX is not asked.

cantoria.program.markdownDescription: For developers: the `cantoria` program to run instead of the one bundled with this extension (a build from the repository).
